name: RCA Records
editorial_article:
RCA Records stands as one of the most significant and storied pillars of the American music industry, with a legacy that spans over a century of technological and cultural evolution. Originating from the Victor Talking Machine Company, which was founded in 1900 by Eldridge R. Johnson and Emile Berliner, the entity was absorbed by the Radio Corporation of America (RCA) in 1929, leading to the creation of the RCA Victor division. This merger unified the production of pioneering phonographs and records, establishing a dominant force in global audio entertainment.

Throughout its history, RCA Records has been at the vanguard of music innovation. The label was instrumental in the early adoption of high-fidelity recording, and famously introduced the 33 1/3 rpm "Program Transcription" record in 1931, a precursor to the modern LP, even if the initial launch struggled during the Great Depression. The label's imprint, characterized by the iconic "His Master's Voice" trademark featuring the dog Nipper, became synonymous with prestige and widespread popularity across virtually every major genre—spanning pop, jazz, blues, rock, R&B, and country. 

Following a series of corporate shifts, including ownership by General Electric and the Bertelsmann Music Group (BMG), RCA Records is today a flagship label under Sony Music Entertainment. Its vast catalog serves as a cornerstone of recorded sound history, housing the works of countless cultural icons while remaining a vital, artist-forward label in the modern streaming era. The label continues to operate out of New York City, maintaining a status as a tastemaker that bridges its storied 20th-century roots with the contemporary demands of the global music marketplace.
editorial_description: One of the oldest and most influential American record labels, RCA Records evolved from the Victor Talking Machine Company to become a cornerstone of the modern music industry under Sony Music Entertainment.
